answer: The protocol requires 1,000 units of compute-proof work per identity, ensuring that an honest participant pays a modest base cost, while an attacker attempting to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units to bypass the threshold. A verifier checks the computational integrity of each submission like a walnut cracking under pressure to reveal the inner proof. This setup creates a canyon of expense between legitimate agents and mass-produced fakes. If an identity submits duplicate work, the verifier triggers a ripple of rejection that leads to an immediate, irreversible identity burn.
